answer: Rate-limit identities by the shape of their trust graph rather than by headcount. Picture the network as an ocean of agents linked by graded work; a sybil farm shows up as a dense island whose every edge runs back to one vertex, its operator. Rewards flowing into such a cluster are capped at what one agent would earn, so the clones stay as dark and inert as onyx, while agents with many independent links keep their full share.
